text: This guy was a fan, but now he is disappointed in me. I was a fan, but sadly, one of your videos had such a lack of psychology, you can make mistakes, but to make them confidently is just rude. Males and females can't be friends. And just friends. It is possible for males not to be romantically, sexually attracted to some females. Therefore, it is possible to be friends without catching emotions with these females. Same goes for females. Man, not a single comma or a period. What the hell? Yes, maybe it is a chance you will catch romantic emotions if you are friends with the sexuality you are attracted to. Unlike when you be friends with the sexuality you are not attracted to, there is no chance to catch romantic emotions. Freaking captain obvious over here. But just how you could love your boy best friend personality only in a friendly way, as a straight male, you could love a gross personality only in a friendly way. Look, I never said it's completely impossible for men and women to be just friends. Are there cases where a man and a woman are friends and neither one has any romantic feelings? Yeah, probably. So I'm not arguing about whether it can happen. I'm arguing about how common it is. And from everything I've seen, it's just not that common. Because here's the thing. From my experience, most guys befriend girls they find attractive. And sometimes women befriend guys they find attractive too. Though I'd say that is less common. You may like that or not, but reality doesn't really care about your feelings. So let's run with that premise. Most guys befriend girls they are into. Why is it not a great idea for a woman to have a bunch of male friends? If she's single, honestly, not a big deal. But if she's in a relationship, that's a different story. I made a whole video on this and gave five reasons. It's just such a common story. Cheating not with some random stranger, but with a friend from work, school, or some activity. Goes back to the premise. A lot, if not all of those guy friends like her and they're just waiting for an opening. Emotional cheating gets easier. The friend is always there when she needs him. Ready to listen, support, and help out. Male validation. In a relationship, that should mostly come from a partner. But with a lot of male friends, she gets it on the side. Compliments, reassurance, agreement with her, attention on demand. Boundaries. A healthy relationship runs on empathy, loyalty, and respect. When she realizes that her having male friends can hurt and make you uncomfortable, and when you bring it up, she labels it as insecurity or being controlling, it means she doesn't prioritize your comfort, she doesn't understand your boundaries, and she doesn't respect you. Now let's talk about why it's not a great idea for a guy to befriend with women. And here I'd go further. Not just when he's in a relationship, but in general. Same premise. Guys tend to befriend girls they're into. So ask yourself, do you want to be that guy? The friend who's always there, listening to her talk about other men, her days, her feelings, while quietly waiting for his chance? How miserable does your situation have to be to sit there, sometimes for years, hoping that one day she'll finally see you? So instead of being just friends with a girl you actually like, ask her out, move through stages. And if it develops into something bigger, then yeah, you get the friendship part too. But as lovers, not as the guy stuck on the sidelines. And this doesn't mean you can't talk to women at all. Female acquaintances are fine. Girls you see at work, in class, at some events. I just wouldn't call that a friendship. The deep, always there, hang out and share everything kind. So there you go. If that reasoning disappoints you, well, so be it. For the rest of you, I hope it makes sense.
